edit.description: snapshotReverted's catch warns through the store's own logger before returning
the warn case, driven by a capture that throws

summary: a failed reverted-prose snapshot reaches no log, record or note, so nothing says the recovery artifact is gone
acceptance: A snapshotReverted whose listing, read or write throws emits one warn naming the snapshot dir and the underlying error, and the revert still proceeds and still returns.
tests: a failed reverted-prose snapshot warns with the directory it could not write
notes: src/priorAttempts.ts:732-733 — a bare `catch {}`, no log, while writeRevertNote on the same revert path warns (src/tickAttempt.ts:861). The store already holds a Logger (:348). Per spec/worktrees.md, *Reverted prose survives the reset*: "Recovery must never require reading session logs" — silence makes the session log the only route and the operator does not know to look. A warn neither blocks nor fails the revert, which is the whole of what that section's best-effort clause rules out.
